messages:
anya: Heads-up — noticed a sharp uptick in long-context requests from prod-region-eu over the last 24h, looks correlated with streaming chat usage. p95 token length went from ~1.2k to ~4.6k.

sam: whoa. any idea if this is a single customer or broad?

anya: quick slice: top 5 api_keys account for 68% of the increase, but there are also many small clients nudging up. Mainly chat streaming endpoints.

jordan: metrics I pulled: tokens_in_per_min spiked ~3x during peak window, tokens_out also up but less, so net GPU hours jumped ~2.1x on the affected pools.

maya: dump the query please — want to cross-check against batching rates and GPU utilization.

jordan: paste: ```promql
sum(rate(redwood_requests_tokens_total{env=\"prod\",region=\"eu\"}[5m])) by (pool)
```
Results attached in dashboard (link) — pool-gpu-48 and pool-gpu-72 are highest.

liam: infra-bot shows autoscaler reacted but avg batch size shrank from 18 -> 7 because of longer sequences, so throughput per-GPU fell.

anya: correct — KV cache hit rate also dropped (context growth makes cache less reusable), so more memory bandwidth and compute per request.

sam: short-term mitigations?

maya: options: 1) temporarily route streaming-heavy traffic to dedicated pools with larger memory (reduce contention), 2) raise per-key rate limits for non-critical customers to throttle, 3) enable prefix-KV region cache for chat sessions (experimental), 4) increase reserved capacity for eu for next 48h.

liam: cost impact: rough back-of-envelope — if current pattern holds, monthly GPU-hours for eu could +45% => $Xk extra. Need approval for short-term commit increase.

anya: also consider aggressive caching eviction + session compaction at the app layer (truncate history for low-priority chats). Could ask growth to roll out a soft prompt-length cap for free tier.

sam: what about model-level switches? Moving some chat traffic to a 4-bit quantized variant would save ~20% GPU time on long sequences. Any concerns on quality regressions?

jordan: we have a verified quant profile for the chat model; small degradation at long tails, but for streaming it's usually acceptable. Need canary and eval on our prompt-set.

maya: immediate steps I propose: (A) prewarm two extra eu dedicated slots (owner: liam) for 6h, (B) add an alert for median sequence length >2.5k (owner: anya), (C) ask growth to soft-cap free-tier contexts to 3k with notice (owner: sam), (D) schedule canary of quant-4 model on 5% of streaming traffic (owner: jordan).

liam: prewarm command I used earlier: ```sh
# allocate 2x n1-dedicated-gpu
redwoodctl pools create --name temp-eu-boost --gpu-type a100-40 --count 2 --reserved 6h --tags auto-burst
```
I started that at 1766012500.

infra-bot: deploy job temp-eu-boost started by liam at 1766012500, status: provisioning.

anya: can we also tweak batching heuristics — allow dynamic batch timeout increase on streaming endpoints to try to recover batch sizes without hurting latency too much?

liam: yes, we can bump streaming_batch_timeout from 20ms -> 40ms for 2h window. I'll toggle and monitor p95 latency.

sam: planner note — we should update next week's capacity forecast: assume 30% baseline growth in avg context length for Q4 and model streaming adoption +15%. This changes GPU-hour forecast significantly. I'll add a line item to the capacity deck.

jordan: I'll run a simulation overnight: project GPU-hours under 3 scenarios (conservative/moderate/aggressive) factoring in batch size drop and cache hit delta. Will post numbers by 1766016400.

maya: thumbs up. also add regional cost delta: routing to us-east yields cheaper spare capacity but higher egress for EU customers. Need product input.

anya: thanks team — for now monitor the alert, liam watch p95 latency and billing, jordan post the sim, sam coordinate customer comms for any soft caps.

liam: got it. toggled batch timeout at 1766012605.

jordan: simulation job started 1766012700.

sam: I'll draft a 24h note for ops and growth so customers aren't surprised if we change caps.

anya: nice work. let's reconvene if numbers don't show recovery by EOD. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
